definition: Gibbard’s package near truth minimalism additionally requires fitting a maximally specific way things are (equivalently a fully opinionated observer agrees or disagrees). Normative truth concerns what to do; this does not posit a uniform relation represents as its explanation. He excludes false-antecedent indicative conditionals from full truth while allowing lighter truth-like packages.
